working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: County Down is Northern Ireland's most celebrated golf county, anchored by one of the world's most famous links, but the itinerary becomes far more interesting (and more honest about your bank balance) when you add Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle. This post maps out a practical three-course County Down circuit for UK visitors who want to make the most of the trip beyond a single bucket-list round.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (Championship), Newcastle, County Down: consistently ranked among the top 5 courses in the world; par 71, 7,186 yards; set between the Mourne Mountains and Dundrum Bay/Irish Sea; visitors welcome but advance booking essential; two courses on site — Championship Links and the shorter Annesley Links (par 66, 4,548 yards; redesigned by Mackenzie & Ebert in 2015 per top100golfcourses.com); green fees for 2026 reported variously — figures conflict across sources (one source says £450 for 2026, another says £185–£220 peak season, another says £425 for 2025); DO NOT state a specific 2026 green fee as confirmed — describe as 'premium/top-tier' and direct readers to the official site (royalcountydown.org) for current pricing.
- Ardglass Golf Club: clifftop links on the northeast coast of County Down, established 1896; 18 holes, par 70, approx 6,268 yards; clubhouse is a medieval fortified building (c.1405, described as one of the oldest buildings in the world used as a golf clubhouse); approximately 30 minutes from Royal County Down at Newcastle, under an hour from Belfast; open to visitors, tee times bookable direct; frequently cited as a 'must-play add-on' to Royal County Down; green fees reported around £160–£220 peak season in 2025/2026 range — again figures vary, describe as 'significantly less expensive' than RCD and direct to ardglassgolfclub.com; described by multiple sources as slipping under the radar of visitors focused solely on RCD.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: links on the Ards Peninsula, Cloughey village, County Down; founded 1902; course significantly shaped by James Braid in 1934; par 70 (some sources say 69), approx 6,167 yards; described as the most easterly 18-hole course in Ireland; nearest links course to Belfast (approx 45 minutes by road); 'Open Championship' style links with strategic/precision emphasis; par-4 10th at 435 yards cited as one of the most difficult par 4s in Irish golf; course rarely closes due to quick-drying links terrain; recognised as 'Best Value Golf Experience in Ulster'; visitors welcome, open to public.
- Getting there from UK mainland: fly into Belfast City or Belfast International, both within easy reach of County Down (Belfast City closer; approx 16km to Bangor area, c.45 min to Newcastle); ferry options — Cairnryan (Scotland) to Belfast with Stena Line, approx 2 hrs 15 min; Liverpool (Birkenhead) to Belfast with Stena Line, approx 8 hours (overnight option available); car recommended for getting around County Down.
- Slieve Donard Resort and Spa in Newcastle is the closest high-end hotel to Royal County Down — factual mention only, no affiliate link.
- County Down's golfing tradition stretches back to 1881 when Royal Belfast Golf Club was founded.
- Ardglass has risen in profile and green fees have climbed accordingly, no longer purely a 'hidden gem' but still a fraction of RCD's cost.
- Kirkistown: 'The Dip' near the first tee was created during WWII airfield construction — unusual historical detail.
- Annesley Links at RCD is a good option for a warm-up or budget round within the same club.
- County Down is distinct from the Causeway Coast/Antrim route (Royal Portrush etc.) — worth flagging as a separate trip.
